title: Santa Maria Tri-Tip Roast
seoTitle: Santa Maria Tri-Tip Roast | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: West Coast tri-tip that slices fast and feeds the whole hall
subtitle: California salt-pepper-garlic rub, oak smoke, and salsa for ten
description: Adapted from classic Santa Maria tri-tip tradition (Amazing Ribs, Weber): tri-tip gets a salt-pepper-garlic rub, smokes over oak at 275°F to 130°F, then sears and slices against the grain with pinquito beans and salsa.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Santa Maria Tri-Tip Roast in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use neutral oil as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season Santa Maria-style
steps.instruction: Mix salt, pepper, and garlic. Coat tri-tip with oil, then pack rub on all sides. Rest 30 minutes while smoker heats to 275°F with oak.

steps.title: Smoke to 130°F
steps.instruction: Smoke tri-tip at 275°F until internal temp reaches 125–130°F for medium-rare, about 45–55 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sear over high heat
steps.instruction: Sear over direct heat at 450°F+ 3–4 minutes per side until crust forms and internal temp reaches 135°F for medium. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes. Slice against the grain into thin slices—tri-tip grain changes direction; rotate as you cut. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Toss slices lightly with warm beef broth. Cover with foil and hold at 170°F until service. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Warm beans and salsa
steps.instruction: Heat pinto beans in a pot. Set pico de gallo cold on the line. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cooking step
steps.instruction: Sliced tri-tip, beans, salsa, optional tortillas. Call temps: pulled at 135°F medium, held at 170°F. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Slice thin for tri-tip sandwiches with salsa and mayo. Reheat in broth at 325°F until 145°F. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Tri-tip grain shifts mid-roast—pay attention when slicing or bites turn chewy.
125°F off smoke + sear gets you medium-rare; push to 130°F before sear for medium.
Oak is traditional; hickory works if that's what's in the pit.
tonightSpread: Sliced tri-tip on a board with jus.
Warm pinto beans, pico de gallo, and tortillas.
leftovers: Tri-tip tacos with salsa and avocado.
Chop into a steak salad with ranch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tri-tip cooks in under two hours and slices like steak night without the cost. Holds sliced at 170°F with jus for 45 minutes.
mealPrepNotes: Season 30 minutes ahead. Smoke to 130°F, sear hot, rest 10 minutes, slice. Hold sliced tri-tip covered at 170°F with beef jus.
